page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance configured with a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Hosted on a KVM hypervisor, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is supported by a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1 data cache. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB (4.0 GB per vCPU). The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external network block volumes, and includes no GPU hardware. Baseline networking capability is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate modest computational performance relative to contemporary cloud instances. Single-core processing demonstrates lower-tier throughput, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 848.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1105.29. Multi-threaded metrics reflect similar positioning, with a PassMark CPU score of 6995.67 and a Geekbench multi-core result of 3291.0. The Intel processor supports standard vector instruction sets including AVX and AVX-512F along with AES-NI cryptographic acceleration, enabling PassMark extended instruction scores of 6054.5.

Subsystem benchmarks reflect moderate bandwidth alongside subdued transactional speeds. Uncached large-block memory operations reach 37.94 GB/sec for reads and 33.29 GB/sec for writes. In application-level testing, the instance achieved a static web serving throughput of 3.58 GB/sec and handled 5.54 million Redis SET operations per second. Machine learning workloads on lightweight 135M parameter models yield average generation rates of 99.85 tokens/sec, but larger models such as 7B decline sharply to 4.89 tokens/sec.

The ecs.sn2.xlarge represents a standard resource profile for horizontal web scaling, internal utility microservices, staging environments, light database services, and general back-office application hosting where moderate dedicated CPU and 32 GB RAM satisfy capacity needs without requiring premium per-core compute performance.

The instance features no local storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators, operating with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.sn2.xlarge is suited for standard enterprise background tasks, staging environments, lightweight relational databases, and distributed web services with predictable, moderate resource requirements.
